points.text: Abstract overclaims provable RO avoidance, many environments, superiority and efficiency over state of the art
Theorem 5.1's hypothesis is its own conclusion
Section 4 asserts links without theorems
Inconsistencies: s-squared direction, notation clash for K, references to nonexistent equations/theorems
Table 1 lacks number of seeds and meaning of plus-minus
Two Modalities results only a qualitative scatter plot; no quantitative score
No efficiency or timing measurement despite efficiency claim
Only low-dimensional environments; no standard cooperative benchmark
Fig. 6 caption copied, Eq. 7.4 lacks gamma, terse related-work phrasing
Theorem 5.1 hypothesis assumes its conclusion
No formal bridge from consistent reasoning to RO avoidance
Finite-action assumption of lemmas violated by continuous-action experiments
Alpha annealing to zero required by theory not satisfied in experiments
Exact SVGD assumption violated by practical implementation
Shared randomness at execution likely removes ERO; baselines lack it
Improvement step and practical gradient not shown to match theory's nested conditionals
Baselines from 2017-2019; no recent RO baselines
Tuning parity with baselines unstated
"Many RO-challenged environments" claim rests on three toy games
Efficiency never measured
SVNR-F matches SVNR, so strict nesting requirement is not tested
Inconsistencies: s-squared direction, MADDPG text vs table, nonexistent equation references
At s-squared 3.0 "highest return" claim is within noise of L-MADRL
Theory for finite action sets while experiments use continuous actions
Alpha schedule ends at positive value, never zero as Theorem 5.2 requires
SVGD convergence invoked for idealized particles; no bound for finite particles or amortized network
Theorem 5.1 nearly circular: assumes convergence to optimal policy
Claim that consistent reasoning implies no RO has no theorem
Baselines old (2017-2019) despite state-of-the-art claim
Only three tiny games used for "many RO-challenged environments"
SVNR gets 50-trial tuning; baselines' tuning budget unstated
Table 1 omits seed count and whether plus-minus is std or variance
s-squared 3.0 difference with L-MADRL within spread yet claimed highest
Efficient computation claimed but never measured
Reproducibility details missing: architecture, chosen hyperparameters, compute, code
Ablation cannot show strict nesting matters since SVNR-F performs on par
No ablation of amortization, rounds K or particles M
Minor: copied caption, missing gamma, wrong equation numbers, limit notation, sum index
Eq. 6.6 improvement step lacks soft marginalization; policy improvement proof unsupported
Practical gradient Eq. 7.2 equals nested conditional only for full conditioning
ERO fix relies on shared random seed, a stronger execution model not given to baselines
Scaling beyond four agents and one-dimensional actions untested
No sampling-quality diagnostic for SVGD against Boltzmann target
Cognitive-science framing and "negotiation" term loosely connected to technical content
Robustness to undelivered shared noise or inconsistent agent ordering not discussed
"Negotiation policy" and "perceived opponent policy" terms used interchangeably
"First provable RO method" claim not differentiated from value-factorization and policy-gradient RO work
Relation to ROMMEO under-argued; no experiment where ROMMEO and SVNR-F differ
Recursive Reasoning Graph not cited
Method resembles autoregressive/sequential coordination schemes, which are not discussed
"Negotiation" and cognitive framing overstate a sequential conditional sampler
No autoregressive-policy baseline with shared randomness
"Provably" applies to idealized algorithm, not SVNR as run
Theorems for finite action spaces but experiments use continuous actions
Communication-free execution claim conflicts with sharing noise between neighbours at test time
Little guidance on schedules and hyperparameter sensitivity
Shift from known-model policy iteration to critic learning not analysed
Compute and tuning parity versus baselines not tabulated
Scope limited to CTDE and full observability
Strictly nested negotiation sets and max-entropy assumptions restrictive; sensitivity unexplored
Training cost, memory and runtime overhead not quantified
Unclear distinction from opponent-modeling and communication-based MARL approaches
No analysis of emerging negotiation dynamics, rounds used, or PRO/ERO evolution
Dense writing; proofs and definitions need intuition or visuals
Guarantees require annealing alpha to zero, unlike practice
Gap between proofs assuming optimal joint policy and amortized neural implementation
Decentralized execution assumes amortization faithfully reproduces multi-round negotiation
Sample efficiency and robustness underexplored; no training curves
Finite action space assumptions mismatch continuous control practice

P.summary: Abstract and intro overclaim scope, environments and superiority
No theorem linking consistent reasoning to RO avoidance
Alpha not annealed to zero as theory requires
Idealized SVGD/particle theory vs implementation; "provably" covers idealization only
Shared randomness at execution drives result; baselines lack it
Practical updates not shown to match theory's nested conditionals
Strict nesting role not supported by ablation
Only toy low-dimensional environments, no standard benchmark
No ablation of amortization, K, M
Robustness to noise delivery and ordering

Q.summary: Finite action theory vs continuous experiments
Shared noise at execution vs communication-free claim
Gap between idealized theory and learned/amortized implementation
Compute and tuning parity not tabulated
Unclear relation to opponent modeling/communication MARL
Sample efficiency and robustness, no training curves
